id: title:cvolzer3:preserve android notification taps during startup

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a native Android bridge and its implementation, documentation, and tests to preserve notification tap responses after process death, a critical reliability and user experience feature for mobile users.
review.reason: The change group adds a substantive, bounded capability: a new Android notification intent plugin and its native implementation. This includes the Gradle module, AndroidManifest, Kotlin service, and Expo autolinking entry, along with documentation and tests. review.uncertainty: While the implementation and tests are present, the complete end-to-end behavior and production deployment status are not independently verified; the score relies on the presence of the implementation and tests rather than observed production outcomes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, complete change group. No unrelated PRs are present. No tier assignment is performed; only observations are returned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new Android notification intent plugin and its native implementation, including a new Gradle module, AndroidManifest, Kotlin service and module, and an Expo autolinking entry.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides a native Android bridge to preserve notification tap responses after process death and to route them before Expo's startup delegate can drop them.

observations.behavior: Adds documentation explaining the Android-specific workaround for notification taps after process death, including the rationale and the need for a new Android build.

observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies the expected behavior and recovery path for notification taps when the app is not running or the user is not authenticated.

observations.behavior: Adds a new section to the testing documentation with commands and test sequences for Android notification taps after process death.
observations.posthog_connection: Defines the new Android module that will be used by the notification intents plugin.
